Let \(f\) be a function that is continuous on the interval [0,4). The function \(f\) is twice differentiable except at \(x=2\). The function \(f\) and its derivatives have the properties indicated in the table above, where DNE indicates that the derivatives of \(f\) do not exist at \(x=2\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] For \(0<x<4\), find all values of \(x\) at which \(f\) has a relative extremum. Determine whether \(f\) has a relative maximum or a relative minimum at each of these values. Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] On the axes provided, sketch the graph of a function that has all the characteristics of \(f\). (Note: Use the axes provided in the pink test booklet.)
(c) Let \(g\) be the function defined by \(g(x)=\int_{1}^{x} f(t) d t\) on the open interval (0, 4). For \(0<x<4\), find all values of \(x\) at which \(g\) has a relative extremum. Determine whether \(g\) has a relative maximum or a relative minimum at each of these values. Justify your answer.

\item[(d)] For the function \(g\) defined in part (c), find all values of \(x\), for \(0<x<4\), at which the graph of \(g\) has a point of inflection. Justify your answer.
\item[(a)] \(f\) has a relative maximum at \(x=2\) because \(f^{\prime}\) changes from positive to negative at \(x=2\).
\item[(b)]
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/9a5d1584-f165-4d52-b44b-0092bd5c4664-1.jpg?height=662&width=679&top_left_y=1482&top_left_x=348)
\item[(c)] \(\quad g^{\prime}(x)=f(x)=0\) at \(x=1,3\).
\(g^{\prime}\) changes from negative to positive at \(x=1\) so \(g\) has a relative minimum at \(x=1 . g^{\prime}\) changes from positive to negative at \(x=3\) so \(g\) has a relative maximum at \(x=3\).
\item[(d)] The graph of \(g\) has a point of inflection at \(x=2\) because \(g^{\prime \prime}=f^{\prime}\) changes sign at \(x=2\).
\end{itemize}
